# relation-without-foreign-key

- Dialects: mysql, postgres, sqlite
- Default: on

## Why

The model relates two tables, and queries and cascades assume the referenced row exists. Without a foreign key the database accepts references to rows that were never created or have been deleted, and those dangling ids surface later as missing data or failed joins. A many-to-many join table needs a foreign key to each side for the same reason.

## Fix

Declare the relation in the model so the generated schema has a foreign key from the referencing columns (for a join table, one to each joined table), then regenerate the migration. Delete or repair orphaned rows first, or the constraint cannot be added.

## Exception

Relations deliberately kept without a constraint, for example across a sharded boundary, to a table in another database, or on a table that is bulk loaded; write the reason down.

The same text is printed by `schemalens explain relation-without-foreign-key`. An exclusion needs a written reason. Back to the [rule index](README.md).
